subject.title: Feature: Native Audio Input for Omni-Modal Models (skip STT transcription)

question: Should OpenClaw add opt-in native audio model input for inbound channel audio now, and what provider, fallback, raw-media egress, and transcript/audit contract should govern it?
rationale: The feature aligns with multimodal provider direction, but it changes core model content types, provider serialization, raw voice-byte egress, config surface, and durable session semantics; those choices require maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Design Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue as the canonical tracker and require an approved typed audio/provider/security/session contract before accepting implementation.

options.title: Adopt A New Implementation PR
options.body: Invite a fresh PR only after it proves the typed contract, default STT compatibility, provider fallback, and real Telegram or WhatsApp voice-note behavior.

options.title: Defer Native Forwarding
options.body: Keep batch audio transcription as the supported path until a missing plugin/provider API or stronger maintainer demand justifies raw audio forwarding in core.

recommendation.title: Design Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the canonical tracker and require an approved typed audio/provider/security/session contract before accepting implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal across inbound media understanding, model prompt content, and embedded runner surfaces points to this owner for the design decision.
